data.title: Stage 2 code review
body: # Stage 2 code review
- **Scope:** 5,753 lines, 383 tests
- **Method:** five axes — correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance
## Fixed during the review
| Finding | Action |
| **Templates covered by no test at all** — 4 functions, zero checks | +15 tests; found that `template save` silently accepted non-existent fields |
| `parseDuration` untested, although it takes user input | +4 tests on edge cases, including `0` and `2 days` |
| The renderers `renderTaskTree`, `renderCycles`, `colorsEnabled` untested | +5 tests; among them a check that the tree **survives a cycle** rather than looping forever |
| `currentBranch()` — dead code | removed |
## Accepted as debt, deliberately not touched before the release
| Problem | Why not now |

| **`runBoardUi` — 689 lines in a single function** | The crudest violation. But this is UI code that has just been stabilised after four bugs; taking it apart before the release means risking exactly what has only just started working |
| **`task.ts` — 998 lines**, at the edge of health | A mechanical split into `task/read.ts` and `task/write.ts` is safe, but touches 12 imports. After the release |

| `apply()` in projection — 209 lines, a large `switch` | This is an event dispatcher: splitting it into a function-per-event adds 12 small functions and does not reduce the number of concepts in the reader's head |
| `runTaskEdit` — 118 lines with a nested loop | The "compare every field" logic really is long; worth extracting into `diffFields()` |
**Rationale for the pause:** the skill says plainly to separate refactoring from other work. A release is a fixing of what works; a large UI refactor does not belong in it.
## Axes where no problems were found
- **Security.** No network, no secrets, no external input beyond CLI arguments and journal files — both validated at the boundary. `npm audit` is clean: one runtime dependency.
- **Performance.** Guardrails under tests; the worst case (10k events without compaction) is documented as a limit, not as a promise.
- **Correctness.** 383 tests, including integration tests against real git.
## A blind spot worth naming

Across three iterations with the TUI, four bugs were found, and **not one was caught by the tests** — all of them surfaced on a manual run. The shared trait: code at the boundary with the environment (terminal, focus, key stream).

Partly closed by extracting key routing into a pure function (`src/tui/keys.ts`, 15 tests). The rest of the TUI stays under manual verification — an automated test of terminal interaction needs a pty harness, and that is separate work.
